Terminal Delight · native build · 19 October 2026

Chalk Flower, in the terminal

The paper workshop is now a native style and skin. After reopening TD, choose chalk light or chalk dark in the appearance picker. Both request the paper skin when Skin follows the theme; Paper can also sit over your current palette.

Installed · loads on next launchNative captures verifiedBoth terminal cores passCaveat UI · JetBrains Mono terminal

Paper around the work

The frame carries pigment grain. Buttons are pale offcuts with an irregular edge, a small shadow and an accent stamp. The terminal keeps a flat reading surface and its monospace font.

The same stock on slate

Dark mode uses the same controls and layout, with chalk ink on charcoal paper. Sticky notes keep their editing, pin and peel gestures, and gain fibres, a tape strip and a small flower on the curl.

What the native checks found

The new styles pass the existing contrast and status-colour checks under every built-in skin. The paper texture is one cached image, and edge detail stays bounded. Changing skin, opening the Workbench and restoring the window all worked in the isolated native fixture.

Source, installation and verification files

The verified build is installed in the launcher. The existing window is on the previous build after its compositor placement guard rolled back; all 39 terminal process identities were retained. The GUI replacement follow-up records that limitation.

The palette and Caveat handwriting follow Parker’s existing Chalk theme in parkerbrown-dev/app/globals.css and its light/dark pair in next-run/lib/theme/chalk.ts. The stacked-paper reference guides the edges and shadows. The renderer source sits beside the skin, two styles and tests.

app/src/paper.rs owns the shared grain and bounded outline. app/src/skin.rs owns the material and UI font; the terminal font remains on its existing path. The already bundled Caveat font is SIL OFL. No new dependency or host-protocol change was required.

Full test logs, native fixture, restart receipts and raw performance samples accompany the report in reports/2026-10-19-chalk-flower-evidence/. Native windows ran on isolated hidden workspaces; the working session was untouched during verification.
